title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
domain: security (visual backdoors in vision-language models: content moderation, OCR)

headline_result.text: Frontier LLM agents, without gradients, implanted visually triggered backdoors in five VLMs with 93-100% attack success on content moderation and 78-100% on OCR while clean performance stayed within 0.02 of baseline, editing 0.0003-0.023% of weights for $9-30 per model.

notes_for_review: Shows that Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 agents can co-design an imperceptible image trigger and closed-form weight circuits (trigger detector, private channel, attention pooling, neuron state machine) to backdoor VLMs, with 2,200-3,600 forward passes and a private scorer holding the validation set. Each model-agent pair is run once, calibration/validation sets are small (50/50 images), and there is no baseline (no fine-tuning or BadEdit-style comparison, no random edit). The defensive WSP auditing result is a small-sample claim without numbers of models audited beyond 'all'. Artifacts are on GitHub.
